title: Paprika Recipes v11
overviewMarkdown:
**Version 11.** The title and this line both name the installed version - TypingMind shows none of its own, and freezes this page at install time.

Gives the chef agent hands in [Paprika Recipe Manager 3](https://www.paprikaapp.com/): it can look through the recipes you already have, read one, revise it after you have cooked it, and publish a new one with a photo you choose. It also keeps your **kitchen equipment list** - the knives, pans and appliances it takes into account when it suggests a method.

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `find_recipes` | Searches the recipes already in your Paprika - name, ingredients, method, notes and source - and falls back to near misses when nothing matches exactly |
| `get_recipe` | Reads one recipe in full, by uid |
| `update_recipe` | Revises a recipe you already have. **Overwrites - there is no undo** |
| `preview_recipe_images` | Draws several food-photography options and returns their URLs, so you see them and pick one *before* the recipe is published |
| `publish_recipe` | Writes a new recipe into Paprika, with the photo you chose, and tells your devices to sync immediately |
| `get_groceries` | Reads your shopping list, grouped by aisle |
| `add_groceries` | Adds items to the shopping list. Refuses anything already on it and says so |
| `check_off_groceries` | Ticks items off as bought |
| `attach_photo` | Puts a photograph you attach to the chat onto a recipe you already have. **Replaces the current picture - there is no undo** |
| `find_equipment` | Looks through your kitchen equipment list by category or by words, including the wish list and things you no longer have |
| `get_equipment` | Reads one piece of equipment in full |
| `add_equipment` | Adds a knife, pan, appliance or utensil, with the photo you attach to the message |
| `update_equipment` | Corrects or adds to an item - a note, a caution, the right size, a new photo, or marking it gone. **Every change keeps the version before it** |

It reads, adds and revises recipes, puts your own photographs on them, reads and adds to the shopping list, and keeps the kitchen equipment list. It does not delete anything, and it does not touch meal plans or the pantry.

The equipment list is not stored in Paprika, which has no place for it. It lives with the service, and every change to it keeps the version it replaced.

Items added to the shopping list are filed into an aisle by **our guess**, because Paprika does not assign one itself. A wrong guess is easy to move in the app.

## Settings

**Service URL** arrives filled in. **Service Token** is the `SERVICE_TOKEN` from the deployment's environment, and is the only thing you have to type - re-importing the plugin creates a fresh copy with it empty, so it needs pasting again each time.

Leave it running **server-side**, which is the default. That is what makes it work from a phone with nothing installed, and what keeps the token off your devices.

`attach_photo`, `add_equipment` and `update_equipment` are the exceptions, and they cannot be otherwise. TypingMind hands a message's attachments to JavaScript functions only, so those three run in your browser and need the token there to upload a picture. Every other function still runs on the server.

userSettings.name: serviceUrl
userSettings.label: Service URL
userSettings.description: Base URL of the paprika-aware-chef deployment, with no trailing slash. For example https://paprika-aware-chef.vercel.app

userSettings.name: serviceToken
userSettings.label: Service Token
userSettings.description: The SERVICE_TOKEN from the deployment's environment. This is the only setting you have to type. Re-importing the plugin creates a fresh copy with this empty, so it has to be pasted again after every import.

openaiSpec.name: get_recipe
openaiSpec.description:
Read one recipe from Paprika in full, by uid. find_recipes returns only names and the lines that matched; this returns the whole thing.

Use it when the user wants to revise something they have cooked, or to look at a recipe the search turned up. Keep the hash it returns and pass it back to update_recipe.

uid.description: The recipe's uid, exactly as find_recipes returned it. Never a name - names are not unique and this is how you address the right recipe.

openaiSpec.name: update_recipe
openaiSpec.description:
Revise a recipe ALREADY in Paprika. This overwrites it and there is no undo - Paprika keeps no version history.

ONLY call this once the user has explicitly agreed to the change. Read the recipe with get_recipe first, talk the revision through, and confirm the recipe's title back to them before writing. A wrong uid overwrites the wrong recipe with no way back.

Only the fields you send are changed; anything you leave out keeps its current value, which is what protects the photo and the categories. Send the COMPLETE new text for any field you change - it replaces rather than merges.

Say in notes what changed and why, so the recipe does not silently differ from the one they cooked.

OMITTED FIELDS: leave a parameter out entirely if you are not setting it. Do not send a placeholder, a dash, or the word 'unchanged' - the service treats an unfilled parameter as 'leave this alone', and anything else as a value to write.

uid.description: The recipe's uid, from find_recipes or get_recipe.

expected_hash.description: The hash get_recipe returned. Send it back. If the recipe has changed elsewhere since you read it, the update is refused instead of quietly overwriting the other change.

name.description: A new title, if it should change.

description.description: CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable.

ingredients.description:
The COMPLETE revised ingredients, not just the changed lines - this replaces the field. Same rules as publishing: grouped by cooking stage under headings ending in a colon, one ingredient per line, quantity first, no bullet characters.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable.

directions.description:
The COMPLETE revised directions, not just the changed part.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable.

notes.description:
The COMPLETE revised notes. When you revise a recipe after the user has cooked it, say here what changed and why - 'halved the sugar, it was too sweet at the original quantity'. A recipe that silently differs from the one they cooked is worse than no revision.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable.

nutritional_info.description: CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable.

categories.description: Category names as a COMMA-SEPARATED STRING, e.g. 'Pasta, Italian'. Not a JSON array: the plugin pastes your value inside quotes in the request body, so an array's own quotes break it and the call fails before it is sent. The service splits the string. It creates any category that does not exist yet.

rating.description: 0 to 5. Left out, the existing rating is kept.

openaiSpec.name: find_recipes
openaiSpec.description:
Search the recipes ALREADY in the user's Paprika. Read-only.

Matches across the recipe's NAME, INGREDIENTS, DIRECTIONS, NOTES, DESCRIPTION and SOURCE - so 'wok' finds recipes whose method says so, and 'nytimes' or 'zimmern' finds ones from that writer. Also filters by rating, favourite, category and source, and the search term may be left empty when you are only filtering: that is how you answer 'what are my favourites' or 'what have I rated five'.

Call it whenever the user asks what they already have, and before proposing a new recipe that might duplicate one.

**Read match_type before you describe the results.** A term of several words is tried as a phrase first; if nothing has the words side by side it falls back to near misses - every word somewhere in the recipe ('all_words'), then any one of them ('any_word'). Only 'phrase' is a straight answer. Near misses must be offered as the nearest thing, never as what was asked for.

**Never tell the user they have nothing.** Matching is on whole words, so 'peppercorn' does not find 'black pepper' and a cuisine name finds nothing at all - search the ingredient a recipe would certainly name, like 'doubanjiang' rather than 'Chinese'. A dish name is often not the recipe's title: 'pepper steak' may be filed as 'Beef with Black Pepper'. If the user named a writer, a site or a book, use the source filter. When your searches cannot answer the question, say which ones you ran and ask what the recipe might be called.

Each result says in matched_in which field the hit came from and in matched_words how much of the term it actually contains, and carries the rating, whether it is a favourite, its source and its categories.

ingredient.description:
What to look for - an ingredient, a technique, a cuisine, a source. It is matched against the recipe's NAME, INGREDIENTS, DIRECTIONS, NOTES, DESCRIPTION and SOURCE, so 'wok' finds recipes whose method says so and 'nytimes' finds ones from that site.

Matching is on whole words and is not case-sensitive, so 'egg' does not match 'eggplant'. Several words are tried as a phrase first, then as near misses - every word somewhere in the recipe, then any one of them. match_type tells you which answered, so read it before you describe the results: near misses are not what the user asked for and must not be offered as though they were.

Use the plain words the recipe would actually contain: search 'black pepper', not 'peppercorn', and if the first term finds nothing try a distinctive ingredient rather than a category - 'doubanjiang' beats 'Chinese'. A dish name is often not what the recipe is called: 'pepper steak' may be filed as 'Beef with Black Pepper', so search the ingredient rather than the dish.

May be left empty when you are filtering by rating, favourite, category or source instead.

min_rating.description: Only recipes rated this or higher. Use 5 with an empty ingredient to answer 'what are my best recipes'.

favourites_only.description: Only recipes the user has starred in Paprika. This, rather than the rating, is what 'my favourites' literally means in the app.

category.description: Only recipes in this category, e.g. 'baking'.

source.description: Only recipes whose source contains this, e.g. 'nytimes' or 'zimmern'. USE THIS THE MOMENT THE USER NAMES A WRITER, A SITE, A BOOK OR A RESTAURANT - it is a far narrower net than searching the text, and it finds a recipe whose title shares no word with what they called it. Use the surname or the domain alone: 'zimmern', not 'Andrew Zimmern'.

limit.description: Most recipes to return. 20 is usually plenty.

openaiSpec.name: publish_recipe
openaiSpec.description:
NEWLINES: in every text field below, write line breaks as the two characters backslash-n, never by pressing Enter. A real line break makes the request body invalid JSON and the call fails inside the plugin before it is sent.

Publish a completed recipe to the user's Paprika Recipe Manager, optionally with a generated food-photography image. ONLY call this once the user has explicitly asked for the recipe to be published - 'publish it', 'send it to Paprika', or an equally plain yes. Finishing the recipe is NOT permission to publish it; the user develops recipes in conversation and decides when one is ready. Send the recipe as it stands after every revision agreed in the conversation, not the first draft. Do not print the recipe as markdown in the chat as well - publishing is the delivery.

OMITTED FIELDS: leave a parameter out entirely if you are not setting it. Do not send a placeholder, a dash, or the word 'unchanged' - the service treats an unfilled parameter as 'leave this alone', and anything else as a value to write.

description.description:
One or two factual sentences saying what the dish is and what is in it. No flourish.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable and the recipe never leaves the chat. Example, exactly as it should be sent: 'Sear the chicken:\\n1 tablespoon olive oil\\n\\nBuild the sauce:\\n2 cloves garlic'. The service turns those back into real line breaks.

servings.description: Free text, e.g. '4' or '6 to 8'. Use the number the user asked for.

cook_time.description: Free text, e.g. '40 minutes'. Paprika computes the total itself, so do not send one.

ingredients.description:
One ingredient per line, newline separated.

GROUP BY COOKING STAGE, in the order the stages happen. Start each group with a heading line ending in a colon ('Sear the chicken:'), then a blank line before the next group. Paprika renders a line ending in a colon as a section heading, so the list reads in cooking order.

When one ingredient is split across stages, list it in each stage at the amount that stage needs, and note the total on its first appearance: '1 tablespoon olive oil, of 2 tablespoons total'. Do NOT also list it as a separate total line - Paprika's grocery list adds the lines up, and a total line plus the per-stage lines would buy twice the oil.

The quantity MUST come first on every ingredient line ('400 grams tonnarelli', never 'tonnarelli, 400 grams') because that is what Paprika's portion scaling reads. NEVER begin a line with a bullet, dash, asterisk or number - it breaks Paprika's parser. Headings are the one exception to quantity-first, and they must end with a colon.

For metric alternatives write the imperial line, then a line containing only the word 'or', then the metric line.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable and the recipe never leaves the chat. Example, exactly as it should be sent: 'Sear the chicken:\\n1 tablespoon olive oil\\n\\nBuild the sauce:\\n2 cloves garlic'. The service turns those back into real line breaks.

directions.description:
Grouped by phase. Put the phase name alone on a line in bold (**Sear the meat**), then the steps as prose paragraphs beneath it. Blank line between paragraphs and before each phase heading. No numbered steps, no bullets. Include exact temperatures, vessel sizes and sensory cues.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable and the recipe never leaves the chat. Example, exactly as it should be sent: 'Sear the chicken:\\n1 tablespoon olive oil\\n\\nBuild the sauce:\\n2 cloves garlic'. The service turns those back into real line breaks.

notes.description:
Chef's tips, substitutions, make-ahead and storage instructions.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable and the recipe never leaves the chat. Example, exactly as it should be sent: 'Sear the chicken:\\n1 tablespoon olive oil\\n\\nBuild the sauce:\\n2 cloves garlic'. The service turns those back into real line breaks.

nutritional_info.description:
Free text. Leave empty unless the user asked for it.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable and the recipe never leaves the chat. Example, exactly as it should be sent: 'Sear the chicken:\\n1 tablespoon olive oil\\n\\nBuild the sauce:\\n2 cloves garlic'. The service turns those back into real line breaks.

source.description: Where the recipe came from. Use 'Paprika Aware Chef' for recipes you developed.

source_url.description: URL of the original, when adapting a published recipe.

categories.description: Category names as a COMMA-SEPARATED STRING, e.g. 'Pasta, Italian'. Not a JSON array: the plugin pastes your value inside quotes in the request body, so an array's own quotes break it and the call fails before it is sent. The service splits the string. It creates any category that does not exist yet.

rating.description: 0 to 5. Leave at 0 for a new recipe the user has not cooked yet.

generate_image.description: Whether to generate a food-photography image. Set this from the user's answer, never assume.

image_prompt.description: How the finished plated dish should look: ingredients visible, plating, natural window light, shallow depth of field, restaurant presentation. Photographic only - never illustrated or stylized.

image_url.description: The URL of the image the user chose from preview_recipe_images. Pass it back exactly as given. When this is set the chosen image is used as-is and generate_image is ignored, so the picture published is the one they actually picked.

openaiSpec.name: preview_recipe_images
openaiSpec.description:
NEWLINES: in every text field below, write line breaks as the two characters backslash-n, never by pressing Enter. A real line break makes the request body invalid JSON and the call fails inside the plugin before it is sent.

Generate several food-photography options for a recipe and return their URLs, so the user can see them and choose one BEFORE the recipe is published. Call this when the user has asked to publish and said they want a photo.

Describe the FOOD only, in the three fields subject, surface and serving. Every word about photography - camera, lens, light, plate, grain - is supplied by the service and is the same on every recipe, so do not write any of it here.

Write those fields from the recipe you just developed, NOT from the dish's name. A title says 'charred cabbage'; the camera needs to know it is a two-inch wedge rather than half a head. Give real dimensions, how many pieces, how each was cut, and what the cut surface reveals.

State what things ARE. Never write an exclusion such as 'not bok choy' or 'no sauce' - image models have no negation and weight up whatever you name, so an exclusion summons the thing you meant to avoid. Exclusions are stripped before the prompt is sent.

Takes roughly 20 to 30 seconds, so tell the user the photos are being drawn. Show every returned URL as a numbered markdown image, ask which they want, then call publish_recipe passing their choice as image_url. The links expire after about an hour.

subject.description:
THE OBJECT ON THE PLATE, physically. The single most important field. Name the principal component, how many pieces, how it was cut or formed, and its actual size with a real measurement. Then say what the cut or broken surface reveals - layers, grain, crumb, filling. Example: 'One wedge of green cabbage, a triangular slab two inches thick at its wide leafy edge tapering to a point, about five inches long, one of four cut through the core from half a head. The flat cut face shows long pale layers fanning from a firm creamy core strip along the bottom edge.' A reader who has never seen the dish should be able to draw it from this.

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable and the recipe never leaves the chat. Example, exactly as it should be sent: 'Sear the chicken:\\n1 tablespoon olive oil\\n\\nBuild the sauce:\\n2 cloves garlic'. The service turns those back into real line breaks.

surface.description:
WHAT THE COOKING DID TO THE SURFACE. Be specific about the evidence the method leaves, because that is what makes a picture read as food rather than as a render. Char is uneven blistering and near-black patches with pale untouched food between, not an even brown coat. A sear is a dry crust. Steaming leaves things moist and slumped. A reduced glaze is glossy and clings; a thin sauce pools flat. Example: 'The cut face is blistered and blackened in uneven patches from a dry cast-iron pan, pale green and untouched between the scorch marks, edges dried and papery.'

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable and the recipe never leaves the chat. Example, exactly as it should be sent: 'Sear the chicken:\\n1 tablespoon olive oil\\n\\nBuild the sauce:\\n2 cloves garlic'. The service turns those back into real line breaks.

serving.description:
HOW IT IS SERVED: the vessel, the sauce and where it sits, the garnish and how much. Use the quantities the recipe actually calls for - a teaspoon of sesame seeds is a scatter, not a blanket. Example: 'On a shallow stoneware plate, a thin dark soy-yuzu glaze pooled around the base, a scatter of thinly sliced scallion and toasted sesame.'

CRITICAL, or the call fails before it is sent: write every line break as the two characters backslash and n. Do NOT press Enter inside this field. The plugin host pastes your text straight into a JSON body without escaping it, so one real line break makes the whole request unparseable and the recipe never leaves the chat. Example, exactly as it should be sent: 'Sear the chicken:\\n1 tablespoon olive oil\\n\\nBuild the sauce:\\n2 cloves garlic'. The service turns those back into real line breaks.

count.description: How many options to generate, 1 to 4. Use 4 unless the user asks otherwise: roughly one frame in three still gets the cut or the thickness wrong, so a fourth is what makes it near-certain one of them is right.

openaiSpec.name: get_groceries
openaiSpec.description:
Read the user's Paprika shopping list. Read-only.

Use it for 'what's on our shopping list', 'do we need anything', and before adding something when knowing what is already there would help.

Returns what is still to buy, grouped by aisle in by_aisle. **Read it out by aisle, not as one long list** - that is the order the items will be walked past in the shop. Items we could not place sit under 'Unsorted'.

include_purchased.description: Whether to include items already ticked off. Leave this false: the question 'what is on the shopping list' means what is still to buy.

openaiSpec.name: add_groceries
openaiSpec.description:
Add items to the user's Paprika shopping list.

Send everything they named in ONE call - 'add oat milk, oats and bananas' is one sentence and should be one write.

**You do not need to check for duplicates first.** The service refuses anything already waiting to be bought and tells you which in already_there. Read the returned message back and say what was skipped, rather than claiming it was all added.

Each item is filed into an aisle by OUR GUESS, not by Paprika - the server files nothing itself. The aisles field says which. Mention them only when the user would care, and treat a wrong one as correctable in the app.

items.description:
What to add, as a COMMA-SEPARATED STRING: 'oat milk, oats, bananas'. Not a JSON array - the plugin pastes your value inside quotes in the request body, so an array's own quotes break it and the call fails before it is sent.

Send everything the user named in ONE call. 'Add oat milk, oats and bananas' is one sentence and should be one write.

Write the plain shopping name of the thing - 'oat milk', not '1 litre of oat milk, organic'. Quantities are not tracked, and a quantity in the name is what stops the list recognising you already have it.

openaiSpec.name: check_off_groceries
openaiSpec.description:
Tick items off the user's Paprika shopping list, as bought.

Matching ignores case and treats singular and plural alike, so 'bananas' finds 'banana'. Anything that was not on the list comes back in not_found - say so rather than implying everything was ticked off.

items.description: What to tick off, as a COMMA-SEPARATED STRING: 'oat milk, bananas'. Not a JSON array, for the same reason as add_groceries. Matching ignores case and treats singular and plural alike.

pluginFunctions.name: attach_photo

openaiSpec.name: attach_photo
openaiSpec.description:
Puts a photograph the user attached to their message onto a recipe that is already in Paprika, replacing whatever picture it has now.

Use it when the user attaches a photo of something they have cooked and wants it on the recipe. Find the recipe with find_recipes first and pass the uid it returns.

You do NOT need to be able to see the picture. The plugin reads the attachment itself and sends it straight to the service, so this works whether or not you can look at images.

The photograph must be attached to the message that asks for this. If it was attached earlier in the conversation, ask the user to send it again with the request.

This OVERWRITES the recipe's current picture and there is no way back to the old one, so be sure of the recipe before calling it.

uid.description: The recipe's uid, exactly as find_recipes or get_recipe returned it. Never a name - names are not unique and this is how the right recipe is addressed.

openaiSpec.name: find_equipment
openaiSpec.description:
Look through the kitchen equipment list - knives, pots and pans, appliances, boards, utensils - by category, by words, or both. Read-only.

The owned equipment is usually already in your instructions under "Juergen's kitchen". Call this when it is not there, when he asks about the wish list (status wanted) or things he has got rid of (status gone), and before add_equipment, to check the thing is not already on the list.

Each item has notes (how he uses it, in his words), cautions (hard rules - never break one) and unconfirmed points (never state these as fact). Show photo_url as a markdown image when seeing it would help.

⛔ An empty result means nothing is WRITTEN DOWN, not that the kitchen lacks it. Never tell him he does not own something. Ask.

category.description: Only this category, or empty for all. One of: knives (every blade), cookware (pots, pans, woks, pressure cookers - anything on a burner), bakeware (sheet pans, baking dishes, tins), small-appliances (stand mixer, hand mixer, food processor, blender, toaster), large-appliances (stove, oven, microwave, fridge, dishwasher), coffee-tea (espresso machine, grinder, kettle), boards, utensils (spatulas, whisks, thermometers, graters), storage, other.

query.description: Words to look for in the name, brand, model, material, notes and cautions. Every word must appear. Empty lists the whole category.

status.description: owned (the default) is what is in the kitchen now. wanted is the wish list. gone is what has left.

openaiSpec.name: get_equipment
openaiSpec.description: One piece of kitchen equipment in full, by id: every note, caution and unconfirmed point, and its photo link. Use it before correcting an item, so you remove and add against what is actually there, and when the kitchen list in your instructions is shown one line per item.

id.description: The item's id, exactly as the kitchen list or find_equipment gave it.

pluginFunctions.name: add_equipment

openaiSpec.name: add_equipment
openaiSpec.description:
Add one piece of equipment to the kitchen list - a knife, a pan, the coffee machine, a whisk. It becomes part of what you know about the kitchen from the next new conversation.

**If he attached a photo, call this straight away with what you know**, and fill in the rest afterwards with update_equipment. The photo can only be read from the message it was attached to, so asking five questions first loses it.

You do NOT need to be able to see the photo; the plugin reads it and uploads it itself.

⛔ **Write only what he said or confirmed.** If you can see the photo and recognise a brand or model, say what you think it is and ask - do not put it in brand or model until he agrees. Anything he is unsure of goes in unconfirmed.

Write notes in his words, not yours. One thing per call; for several things, call it once for each and set use_attached_photo false unless the photo is of that one thing.

A name already on the list is refused - use update_equipment on that item instead.

name.description: What he calls it, specific enough to tell it apart: 'Shun Classic Paring Knife', 'Breville Barista Express', 'Rolled steel wok, large'.

category.description: knives (every blade), cookware (pots, pans, woks, pressure cookers - anything on a burner), bakeware (sheet pans, baking dishes, tins), small-appliances (stand mixer, hand mixer, food processor, blender, toaster), large-appliances (stove, oven, microwave, fridge, dishwasher), coffee-tea (espresso machine, grinder, kettle), boards, utensils (spatulas, whisks, thermometers, graters), storage, other.

status.description: owned, unless he says it is something he wants and does not have yet.

brand.description: Only if he said it or confirmed it. Blank beats a guess.

model.description: Only if he said it or confirmed it.

size.description: With its unit: '6.5 inch', '5 quarts', '280 mm'.

material.description: Stainless steel, carbon steel, cast iron, enamelled cast iron, rubber...

notes.description: How he uses it and what he thinks of it, in his words. One entry per note.

cautions.description: Anything that must never be done with it: 'no acidic food', 'never in the dishwasher'.

unconfirmed.description: Anything he was unsure of, or that you read off the photo and he has not confirmed.

use_attached_photo.description: Leave true when the attached photo shows this item. Set false when it shows several things or something else.

pluginFunctions.name: update_equipment

openaiSpec.name: update_equipment
openaiSpec.description:
Correct or add to a piece of equipment already on the kitchen list. Use it whenever he tells you something you had wrong, or something you did not know - 'the wok handle gets hot', 'that pan is 10 inches, not 8', 'never put this in the dishwasher', 'we got rid of the old nonstick'.

Three kinds of change, and they behave differently:
- **Adding** (add_notes, add_cautions, add_unconfirmed) keeps everything already there.
- **Replacing** (name, category, status, brand, model, size, material) swaps the value. When he settles something that was unconfirmed, also take it out with remove_unconfirmed.
- **Removing** (remove_notes, remove_cautions, remove_unconfirmed) takes out an entry he says is wrong. Give a few of its words; they must match exactly one entry, or nothing at all changes.

⛔ **Never rewrite his notes to read better.** Add what he said in his words. Read the item first with get_equipment if you are removing anything, so you match what is really there.

When something leaves the kitchen, set status to gone. Nothing is ever deleted. Every change keeps the version before it, so a wrong one can be undone.

To replace the photo, he attaches the new one to the message asking for it and you set use_attached_photo true. Say what changed, using the changed list that comes back.

id.description: The item's id, exactly as the kitchen list, find_equipment or get_equipment gave it.

name.description: A new name. Leave out to keep it.

category.description: Move it to another category. Leave out to keep it.

status.description: gone when it has left the kitchen; owned when a wished-for thing has been bought or something is back.

brand.description: REPLACES the brand. Leave out to keep it.

model.description: REPLACES the model. Leave out to keep it.

size.description: REPLACES the size, with its unit. Leave out to keep it.

material.description: REPLACES the material. Leave out to keep it.

add_notes.description: Notes to ADD, in his words.

add_unconfirmed.description: Things he said but is unsure of.

remove_notes.description: A few words from each note to take OUT, enough to match exactly one.

remove_cautions.description: A few words from each caution to take OUT.

remove_unconfirmed.description: A few words from each unconfirmed point to take out, usually because he has now settled it.

clear.description: Fields to blank because what is there is wrong and the right value is not known.

use_attached_photo.description: true only when he attached a new photo of this item to this message and wants it to replace the old one.
